questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant Using a Laplace Expansion Across a Row
questions.problem:
Compute the following determinant using a cofactor expansion along the $1$st row:

$$
|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}|.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using cofactor expansion along the $1$st row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{11}+0\cdot {C}_{12}+3\cdot {C}_{13}+0\cdot {C}_{14} \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{1+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{21}+1\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{23} \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3+2 \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}|=3\cdot 5=15.
$$

questions.problem:
Compute the following determinant using a cofactor expansion along the $1$st row:

$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & 0 \\ 2 & -4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}|.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using cofactor expansion along the $1$st row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & 0 \\ 2 & -4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}| & =1\cdot {C}_{11}+0\cdot {C}_{12}+0\cdot {C}_{13}+(-1)\cdot {C}_{14} \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{1+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 5 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot (-1)^{1+4}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & -4 & -0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 5 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the first $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 5 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}| & =1\cdot {C}_{21}+5\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{23} \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}|+5\cdot (-1)^{2+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -4 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}|+5|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -4 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(-3-0)+5(-6-4) \\  & =3-50 \\  & =-47\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the second  $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we obtain: 

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{21}+1\cdot {C}_{22}+5\cdot {C}_{23} \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|+5\cdot (-1)^{2+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|-5|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =(0-2)-5(-8-4) \\  & =-2+60 \\  & =58\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & 0 \\ 2 & -4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}|=-47+58=11.
$$

questions.problem:
Compute the following determinant using a cofactor expansion along the $2$nd row:

$$
|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ -7 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}|.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using cofactor expansion along the $2$nd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ -7 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{21}+0\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{23}+3\cdot {C}_{24} \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{2+4}\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 \\ -7 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 \\ -7 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 \\ -7 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{11}+(-1)\cdot {C}_{12}+0\cdot {C}_{13} \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{1+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}-7 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-7 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-7-0 \\  & =-7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ -7 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}|=3(-7)=-21.
$$

Compute the following determinant using a cofactor expansion along the $4$th row:

$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -7 & 4 \\ -2 & 5 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using cofactor expansion along the $4$th row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -7 & 4 \\ -2 & 5 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| & =-2\cdot {C}_{41}+5\cdot {C}_{42}+0\cdot {C}_{43}+0\cdot {C}_{44} \\  & =-2\cdot (-1)^{4+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}|+5\cdot (-1)^{4+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}|+5\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the first $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}| & =(-1)\cdot {C}_{11}+1\cdot {C}_{12}+0\cdot {C}_{13} \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{1+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -7 & 4\end{aligned}|+1\cdot (-1)^{1+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -7 & 4\end{aligned}|-|\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(-4-7)-(-8+2) \\  & =11+6 \\  & =17\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the second  $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we obtain: 

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}| & =1\cdot {C}_{11}+1\cdot {C}_{12}+0\cdot {C}_{13} \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{1+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -7 & 4\end{aligned}|+1\cdot (-1)^{1+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -7 & 4\end{aligned}|-|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-4-7)-(0+0) \\  & =-11-0 \\  & =-11\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -7 & 4 \\ -2 & 5 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|=2(17)+5(-11)=-21.
$$
